did: Home's heavy work, in the Nov 13 coordinator run. A busy box no longer counts against you: when another service holds home's CPU, or the kernel kills something for memory, a Rust Rounds program that runs out of time or loses the runner, and a voice note that runs past its deadline, are not blamed. They are asked again on the next pass, at most three times in a row, and a time measured on a busy box is marked as such (#822, with a new panel on the CALL dashboard). A render that keeps killing its own container is now taken as failed after three restarts nobody asked for, instead of being resumed forever; a deploy's restart doesn't count (#820). Home's compute rules are written down in one place (#823), and the promises that every kill for memory reaches you and that renders take turns are now on the assurance page (some-ui #2914). A render test that fails now and then on CI is labelled priority high, and #827 makes its next failure say why. Codex reviewed most of it before running out of credits; a fresh agent reviewed the rest.

calls.title: How busy the box must be before a result is excused
options: some task waiting for a CPU a tenth of the time or more
a quarter of the time or more
calls.why: A false 'busy' only costs a retry a minute later, while a false 'calm' blames a program or a note for good, so the line leans towards excusing.
calls.undo: Change CONTENDED_SHARE in file_host's contention module.

calls.title: When the box never calms down
options: excuse a program or note three times in a row, then judge it as on a calm box
keep excusing it until the box calms
calls.why: Excusing forever would let a busy box hold the queue for good; the bound keeps it moving and says so with a warning.
calls.undo: Raise NOBODYS in the contention module.

calls.title: The deploy-time check of home's memory caps
options: wait for home's RAM to be published and your word on ollama, then start as a warning
build a check that refuses the deploy now
calls.why: Home's RAM is written nowhere, and the caps include ollama's 8 GB, so a refusing check built blind could stop home's next deploy.
calls.undo: Build the refusing check from #709's plan.
